text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Fuelled by the continuing bond rally, takeover enthusiasm triggered by the St George -Advance Bank merger and a belief that the stockmarket is set to post further gains over the next year, the market surged to an all-time high yesterday, with the All Ordinaries Index closing 26.5 points higher at 2363.3. Page 1.

In a move which, if successful, will create Australia's fifth largest bank, with A$40 billion in assets, St George Bank Ltd yesterday launched its fifth attempt in two years to join the ranks of Australia's banking big league, with a A$2.65 billion cash and scrip offer for Advance Bank Australia Ltd. Page 1.

A A$2.2 billion shakeout of the Australian advertising industry will hand three of the world's largest marketing services conglomerates - North American-based Omnicom, UK-based Cordiant Plc and WPP, who together account for more than A$2 billion worth of the A$4.5 billion Australian industry - direct control of about half the local advertising market. Page 1.

As part of a strategy to spend up to A$200 million in start-up costs on Asian brewing projects and following months of negotiations with potential partners in India and Vietnam, Foster's Brewing Group is close to finalising a new joint venture in South East Asia. Page 19.

The Kalkadoon Dancers Association yesterday moved under cultural heritage law, applying to the Federal Court in Brisbane to seek an injunction preventing a key power line link to MIM Holdings Ltd's giant Ernest Henry project, prompting fears among Queensand's mining industry of another wave of project delays. Page 19.

In a statement issued after a board meeting yesterday, CSR Ltd managing director Geoffrey Kells predicted a 20 percent drop in profit for the first half of 1997 and foreshadowed the building materials giant would cut its interim dividend as trading conditions in its major products worsen. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a deal that will create Australia's fifth largest bank, with total assets of more than A$40 billion, New South Wales-based lender St George Bank Ltd shocked the banking industry yesterday with a A$2.65 billion takeover offer for Advance Bank Ltd. On news of the bid, investors rushed into bank stocks, pushing up the share prices of rival regional players such as Adelaide Bank. Page 19.

After overcoming opposition from Telstra Corp and merchant banker Malcolm Turnbull, who emerged yesterday as a major shareholder, embattled pay-TV operator Australis Media Ltd expects to complete its A$190 million rescue bond issue by next week after winning majority shareholder approval for a raft of crucial conditions yesterday. Page 19.

Speaking after the company's annual general meeting in Melbourne yesterday, Foster's Brewing Group chairman John Ralph revealed the group is looking for joint venture partners in emerging Asian and Indian markets, possibly involving an investment of up to A$80 million. Page 21.

Further successful testing at the Buffalo-1 exploration well on the eastern flank of the exciting Laminaria oil discovery off Western Australia has added to the prospectivity of the area, with BHP reporting yesterday the area has been flowing oil at the rate of 11,790 barrels a day. Page 21.

After threatening on Friday to take legal action against other shareholders who failed to use their "best endeavours" to pursue a public listing of the Ten Group, Jack Cowin and Robert Whyte - who each hold five percent of Ten - have announced they will reserve their threat pending the sale of John Singleton Advertising Ltd's five percent stake in the network. Page 21.

After posting a 5.1 percent rise in net profit to A$54.08 million for the year to July 31, which managing director John Pascoe attributed to stringent cost control and the development of new products, baking and milling group George Weston Foods Ltd warned of another tough trading year. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following the biggest takeover in Australian banking history - St George announced yesterday it will buy fellow New South Wales regional Advance Bank for A$2.65 billion - St George will cut 1,000 jobs and close at least 80 branches within two years in an effort to cut A$140 million from annual expenses and make the takeover a profitable one. Page 1.

Eleven years after he helped Advance convert from a building to society to a bank, former Advance executive Robert Whyte is set to treble his money after reaping a A$66.66 million profit from selling his 6.5 percent stake. Whyte's privately-owned Audant is Advance's single largest shareholder with about 13.2 million shares. Page 25.

After booking a profit of A$204 million in the first half of 1995/96, building materials group CSR yesterday warned shareholders that unless trading conditions improved, the profit for the six months to September 31 would be down by 20 percent, forcing CSR to cut its interim dividend by two cents to 12 cents, franked at a rate of 50 percent. Page 27.

Merchant banker Malcolm Turnbull's Turnbull and Partners and Telstra failed to vote down Australis Media's planned A$190 million bond issue in the U.S. at the company's shareholder meeting yesterday. Telstra lawyer John Atkin said Telstra had voted against all resolutions because the Australis board had failed to properly disclose the terms of the rescue package struck with Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and the satellite facility sharing joint venture with Optus Vision. Page 27.

After completing the acquisition of grocer QIW in June and buying Jewel Food Stores this year, independent wholesaler Davids will probably experience a flattened first-half profit but it is still on track for a full-year profit rise of 20 percent, according to joint managing director John Patten. Page 27.

Foster's Brewing chairman John Ralph said yesterday that the brewer had several investment options under review in Asia, including Vietnam and India, and was willing to spend up to A$80 million on new investment opportunities which would more than likely involve a joint venture and a project with an organisation with existing production facilities. Page 27.
THE AGE

After announcing yesterday that it will buy its fellow New South Wales regional Advance Bank for A$2.65 billion, St George Bank vowed to take on the big four banks, although it will cut 1,000 jobs and close 80 branches within two years in an effort to cut $140 million from annual expenses. Page C1.

In a last-minute bid to capture Joe White Maltings, Ridley Corp last night offered an alternative deal of A$2.36 cash, two Ridley shares and the entitlement to a Joe White 14-cent dividend, in a deal which works out to a total offer of A$5.90 a share compared to its final cash offer of A$5.44. Page C1.

CSR has warned shareholders that early figures indicate a 20 percent drop in first-half profits to about A$160 million, compared with a profit of A$204 million in the previous corresponding period. The building materials group issued a statement yesterday saying that unless trading conditions improved, the company would cut its interim dividend by two cents to 12 cents. Page C2.

Speaking after the Foster's Brewing Group annual meeting, president and chief executive Ted Kunkel confirmed that the company intended to invest about A$200 million in equity in Asia, including possible ventures in Vietnam and India, by the time it finalised its Asian growth strategy. Page C3.

Although he conceded cuts to interest rates would result in a narrowing of margins, with a negative impact on profitability, Bank of Melbourne chairman Christopher Stewart told shareholders at the bank's annual meeting yesterday that satisfactory results were still expected. Page C3.

AI Engineering chief Robert Martin confirmed yesterday that he intended to appeal a decision handed down in the Full Court of the Western Australian Supreme Court last month concerning gold leases south of the Bronzewing mine. If his bid to appeal is successful, the legal dispute could be drawn out for another two years. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
